I farm the same 10.1 mu in a wheat-maize round, so I will plan both crops on the full 10.1 mu. I do not like to gamble with yield. What I will do is close to what I did before, and close to what the steady growers around me do. If fertilizer is a little heavy, I can still bear that cost. If yield falls, that hurts much more. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the main fertilizer under before sowing, and give extra nitrogen when the wheat starts taking off in spring. I have well water, so I will not let the field go dry at the key times. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives a fuller ear here if rain and water keep up. I will keep the wheat stubble, do a lighter tillage job, sow quickly, and feed the maize enough nitrogen because maize eats a lot. I will spray when I see pressure, but in a normal year I will count on about two rounds on each crop. I will not do fancy things. I will follow the way that has kept land like mine producing year after year, with a little care on water and fertilizer so I do not lose the season.
